newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian MPs seek parliament probe in telecom scam.
newsitem.headline: Indian MPs seek parliament probe in telecom scam.

text.p: Indian deputies pressed the government on Tuesday to set up a parliamentary probe into a financial scandal involving former Congress Party communications minister Sukh Ram, officials and deputies said.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the federal police agency leading a corruption probe that has recovered more than $1 million from Sukh Ram's homes, asked him on Monday to return from London before September 10 to face its inquiry.
"The investigations so far suggest that more important people than Mr Sukh Ram are involved," communist deputy Gurudas Dasgupta told parliament on Monday.

Communist lawmakers told Reuters that most non-Congress parties were meeting Home (Interior) Minister Indrajit Gupta later on Tuesday to urge that a Joint Parliamentary Committee be set up to investigate the incident.

Sukh Ram was communications minister in former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's government which ushered in the country's sweeping economic reforms from late 1991. Rao and other Congress leaders face other financial investigations.
He headed India's telecommunications privatisation programme until May.

Last month Rao suspended Sukh Ram from Congress Party membership after senior leaders said the unfolding scandal could harm the party's chances in impending elections in Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state, where polls will begin in late September.
Sukh Ram told the CBI and parliament's lower house Speaker Purno Sangma last week of his inability to leave London for at least two more weeks, citing investigations of a heart problem.
The CBI raided two houses owned by Sukh Ram in July and August and recovered some 36.5 million rupees ($1 million) in cash.

The police agency said then that agents had also arrested a senior official in the communications ministry's finance department and seized huge amounts of cash and jewellery from her home, CBI spokesman S.M. Khan said.

The CBI has filed a case against Sukh Ram accusing him of offering favours to an Indian firm. The case alleged a loss to the government of 16.8 million rupees ($470,000) stemming from the purchase of equipment at inflated prices.
A senior CBI official said he could not confirm news reports that the government was considering reviewing all major purchase contracts that Sukh Ram had sanctioned.
Sukh Ram has consistently denied allegations by opposition political parties that he favoured a little-known firm from his home state, Himachal Pradesh, in the tendering process.
Newspapers quoted him as saying last week that the money recovered from his homes did not belong to him.
Telecommunications industry officials say they were unperturbed by the corruption case, and privatisation plans were unlikely to slow down despite raids on Sukh Ram's homes.
